section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS), a 10-item instrument proposed by Kroon van Diest and Tylka to measure perceived restrictive or critical caregiver messages related to food intake and pressure to eat. The scale has a two-dimensional factor structure (RCM and PEM subscales) and uses a 5-point rating scale, with higher scores indicating greater perceived pressure to eat or food restriction. This is a measurement instrument description rather than a study report with participant data.
